Writing a PR description for a cache invalidation fix in our search service. Marcus needs to review and approve this before we can merge.

diff summary:
- files changed: 7
- lines added: 234
- lines removed: 89
- net: +145

key changes:
- search-cache-manager.ts: rewrote invalidateCache() to use versioned keys instead of TTL-based eviction, added 156 lines
- cache-config.ts: new config for cache version prefix, default is v1
- search-handler.ts: updated to pass cache version on reads and writes, removed old TTL logic
- integration-test/search-cache.test.ts: 12 new test cases covering version bumps, concurrent reads during invalidation, and cache miss recovery
- unit-test/cache-manager.test.ts: 8 new unit tests

test results:
- all 20 new tests passing
- existing test suite: 847 tests, all passing
- manual test on staging: search results refresh within 500ms after invalidation event, was taking up to 5 seconds before

what's not tested:
- there's a potential race condition if two invalidation events fire at the exact same millisecond, the version counter could get out of sync between instances
- this is pretty unlikely in practice but I haven't written a test for it
- would need a dedicated concurrency test harness which we don't have set up yet

performance:
- cache hit rate on staging: 94.2% with new approach vs 91.8% with old TTL approach
- p99 search latency: 120ms, no regression

Turn this into a PR description Marcus can review. He needs to decide if we can merge without the race condition test.

Need a PR description for our database index migration. Lena from SRE needs to review this and she has to decide on the rollback strategy before we run it in prod.

diff summary:
- files changed: 4
- lines added: 178
- lines removed: 23

changes:
- migration-2024-06-08-add-idx.sql: adds composite index on orders(customer_id, created_at, status) - this is the big one, 178 lines because it includes the online schema change wrapper
- order-repository.ts: updated 3 queries to use the new index hints
- benchmark/bench-index-perf.ts: benchmark script for measuring query performance

migration details:
- table: orders, currently 14.2 million rows, growing ~50k/day
- index build on staging (8.1M rows): took 4 minutes 23 seconds
- estimated on prod: 7-8 minutes with the online tool, table stays readable during build

performance numbers from staging benchmark:
- query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE customer_id = ? AND created_at > ? AND status != 'cancelled'
- without index: avg 340ms, p99 1.2 seconds
- with index: avg 12ms, p99 45ms
- write overhead: INSERT went from 3ms to 5ms, acceptable

rollback question:
- if something goes wrong, we can drop the index, takes about 30 seconds
- BUT the query hints in order-repository.ts will be wrong without the index, they'll do full table scans
- so do we: A) deploy code and migration together and accept the risk, or B) deploy code first with index hints conditional on index existing, then run migration
- option B is safer but more complex, adds about 20 lines of conditional logic
- I'm not sure which approach Lena will prefer

Write this up as a PR description for Lena to review.
